/**
 * Generated by `semaprax::public_generic_consumer::typescript_calling`. The
 * Core Wasm calling consumer's ABI wrapper (issue #157) -- the TypeScript
 * analog of the Rust calling consumer's `provider.rs` FFI shim (issue
 * #156). This file is a FIXED template: nothing about a specific
 * descriptor changes it. It imports `FIELD_COUNT` and the codec functions
 * from the per-shape generated `carrier.ts`, and the trusted bytes from
 * `descriptor.ts`.
 *
 * HONEST LIMITATION, stated once here (see `typescript_calling.rs`'s own
 * module documentation for the full accounting). Issue #155's Core Wasm
 * physical adapter (`public_generic_abi::wasm::provider::WasmProvider`) has
 * never been compiled to a real `.wasm` binary exposing an
 * open/input_prepare/call/result_export/release ABI: it is exercised only
 * in-process by Rust test code. No such compiled artifact exists anywhere
 * in this repository for this wrapper to link against the way the Rust
 * calling consumer's `provider.rs` genuinely links against a compiled
 * native provider. The one thing issue #155 *does* name as a real,
 * documented Wasm export is `FIXTURE_ENDPOINT_EXPORT_NAME`
 * ("spx_pg_wasm_endpoint_reverse_bytes_v1"), proven for real only against a
 * genuine `WebAssembly.Memory` by `reverse_probe.mjs`'s narrower,
 * handle-free script.
 *
 * This wrapper therefore keeps the allocator, handle registry, and call
 * lifecycle state HOST-SIDE, in this generated TypeScript -- exactly
 * mirroring `reverse_probe.mjs`'s own host-owned bookkeeping over real
 * `WebAssembly.Memory`, elevated to a bounded exact-LIFO allocator and a
 * private handle registry -- and calls into real, genuinely compiled Wasm
 * bytecode only for that one already-named endpoint export, operating on
 * real linear memory this wrapper allocates, writes, and later zeroes on
 * release. It never reimplements or modifies
 * `public_generic_abi::wasm::provider::WasmProvider`, shares no code with
 * it, and this generator never touches `src/public_generic_abi/wasm/**`.
 * "Do not access private allocator exports or internal record offsets"
 * (issue #157's own wrapper requirement) is honored precisely because there
 * are no such exports to access: the loaded module exports only `memory`
 * and the one endpoint function.
 *
 * Ownership wrapper: `OpaqueHandle` is a private-constructor, `#`-branded
 * class. A raw numeric handle is never exported; a cast through `unknown`
 * cannot forge one (`instanceof` requires a real instance of this exact
 * class, not a structurally similar object). `InputHandle`/`ResultHandle`
 * are the same `OpaqueHandle` type distinguished by the registry's own
 * per-entry `role`; `Provider`'s own `#state` is `"live" | "closed"`.
 */

import {
  FIELD_COUNT,
  decodeOutput,
  encodeInput,
  encodeLeaves,
  locateLeaves,
} from "./carrier.js";
import {
  TRUSTED_BINDING_BYTES,
  TRUSTED_DESCRIPTOR_BYTES,
  TRUSTED_ENDPOINT_EXPORT_NAME,
  verifyDescriptorAndBinding,
  verifyModuleArtifactDigest,
} from "./descriptor.js";
import { SemapraxPublicGenericException } from "./errors.js";
import type { Input, Output } from "./types.js";

const PAGE_BYTES = 65536;
/** 16 MiB, matching `boundary_profile.rs::MAX_TOTAL_PAYLOAD_BYTES`. Restated
 * here rather than imported: this package depends on nothing but its own
 * generated code and the platform. */
const MAX_PAGES = 256;

type EndpointFn = (ptr: number, len: number) => void;

/** Every failure ordinal this wrapper's own pipeline recognizes. Test-only:
 * never part of any production or publication claim (this whole file
 * already carries that blanket claim -- see its module banner). */
export const FAILURE_ORDINALS = {
  AFTER_INPUT_VALIDATED: 0,
  AFTER_INPUT_ALLOCATED: 1,
  AFTER_INPUT_WRITTEN: 2,
  AFTER_ENDPOINT_CALLED: 3,
  AFTER_INPUT_RELEASED: 4,
  AFTER_RESULT_ALLOCATED: 5,
  AFTER_RESULT_WRITTEN: 6,
  AFTER_RESULT_COPIED_OUT: 7,
} as const;

export type FailureOrdinal =
  (typeof FAILURE_ORDINALS)[keyof typeof FAILURE_ORDINALS];

function capacityExceeded(reason: string): SemapraxPublicGenericException {
  return new SemapraxPublicGenericException({
    kind: "capacity-exceeded",
    reason,
  });
}

function carrierRejected(reason: string): SemapraxPublicGenericException {
  return new SemapraxPublicGenericException({
    kind: "carrier-rejected",
    reason,
  });
}

/**
 * A bounded, exact-LIFO bump allocator over one real `WebAssembly.Memory`.
 * Growth is real (`memory.grow`, in real 64 KiB pages); release is real
 * (every byte of a deallocated span is zeroed), matching
 * `reverse_probe.mjs`'s own real allocate/release proof, generalized from
 * one reused span to a real exact-LIFO stack.
 */
class HostAllocator {
  readonly #memory: WebAssembly.Memory;
  #top = 0;
  readonly #stack: number[] = [];
  #liveAllocations = 0;
  #liveBytes = 0;

  constructor(memory: WebAssembly.Memory) {
    this.#memory = memory;
  }

  alloc(length: number): number {
    const start = this.#top;
    const end = start + length;
    const requiredPages = Math.ceil(end / PAGE_BYTES);
    if (requiredPages > MAX_PAGES) {
      throw capacityExceeded(
        "the bounded Wasm linear-memory arena is exhausted",
      );
    }
    const currentPages = this.#memory.buffer.byteLength / PAGE_BYTES;
    if (requiredPages > currentPages) {
      const grown = this.#memory.grow(requiredPages - currentPages);
      if (grown === -1) {
        throw capacityExceeded(
          "WebAssembly.Memory.grow refused to grow the arena",
        );
      }
    }
    this.#stack.push(start);
    this.#top = end;
    this.#liveAllocations += 1;
    this.#liveBytes += length;
    return start;
  }

  dealloc(offset: number, length: number): void {
    const top = this.#stack[this.#stack.length - 1];
    if (top === undefined || top !== offset) {
      throw carrierRejected(
        "a release did not name the exact top-of-stack allocation (exact-LIFO release order violated)",
      );
    }
    this.#stack.pop();
    this.#top = offset;
    this.#liveAllocations -= 1;
    this.#liveBytes -= length;
    // Real release: zero the span for real.
    new Uint8Array(this.#memory.buffer, offset, length).fill(0);
  }

  /** A fresh view, reacquired on every call -- never cached across an
   * `alloc`, which may call `memory.grow` and detach the previous
   * `ArrayBuffer`. */
  view(): Uint8Array {
    return new Uint8Array(this.#memory.buffer);
  }

  liveAllocations(): number {
    return this.#liveAllocations;
  }

  liveBytes(): number {
    return this.#liveBytes;
  }
}

type HandleRole = "input-root" | "result-root";

interface RegistryEntry {
  readonly role: HandleRole;
  readonly offset: number;
  readonly length: number;
}

class HandleRegistry {
  readonly #entries = new Map<string, RegistryEntry>();

  static #key(id: number, generation: number): string {
    return `${id}:${generation}`;
  }

  insert(id: number, generation: number, entry: RegistryEntry): void {
    this.#entries.set(HandleRegistry.#key(id, generation), entry);
  }

  get(id: number, generation: number, role: HandleRole): RegistryEntry {
    const entry = this.#entries.get(HandleRegistry.#key(id, generation));
    if (entry === undefined || entry.role !== role) {
      throw carrierRejected(
        "handle is invalid, stale, released, or names the wrong kind",
      );
    }
    return entry;
  }

  remove(id: number, generation: number, role: HandleRole): RegistryEntry {
    const entry = this.get(id, generation, role);
    this.#entries.delete(HandleRegistry.#key(id, generation));
    return entry;
  }

  size(): number {
    return this.#entries.size;
  }
}

/**
 * An opaque, branded handle. The constructor is private: nothing outside
 * this module can mint one, and a cast through `unknown` cannot forge one
 * either -- `instanceof` still requires a real instance of this class,
 * which a plain object literal (however it is cast) can never be.
 */
export class OpaqueHandle {
  readonly #id: number;
  readonly #generation: number;
  readonly #tag: object;

  private constructor(id: number, generation: number, tag: object) {
    this.#id = id;
    this.#generation = generation;
    this.#tag = tag;
  }

  static mint(id: number, generation: number, tag: object): OpaqueHandle {
    return new OpaqueHandle(id, generation, tag);
  }

  belongsTo(tag: object): boolean {
    return this.#tag === tag;
  }

  id(): number {
    return this.#id;
  }

  generation(): number {
    return this.#generation;
  }
}

const RESULT_ID_OFFSET = 1000;

interface CallState {
  stage: "pending-value" | "pending-result";
}

/**
 * The Core Wasm calling consumer's lifecycle. `Provider.open` verifies an
 * exact descriptor/binding/module pairing before any Wasm allocation;
 * `transform` stages one owned input, calls the real endpoint export over
 * real `WebAssembly.Memory`, and returns an independently decoded, freshly
 * copied result; `close` refuses to close over any live handle.
 */
export class Provider {
  #state: "live" | "closed" = "live";
  readonly #allocator: HostAllocator;
  readonly #registry = new HandleRegistry();
  readonly #calls = new Map<number, CallState>();
  #nextGeneration = 1;
  readonly #endpoint: EndpointFn;
  readonly #tag: object = {};
  #injected: FailureOrdinal | null = null;

  private constructor(memory: WebAssembly.Memory, endpoint: EndpointFn) {
    this.#allocator = new HostAllocator(memory);
    this.#endpoint = endpoint;
  }

  static async open(
    moduleOrBytes: WebAssembly.Module | BufferSource,
    options: { descriptorBytes?: Uint8Array; bindingBytes?: Uint8Array } = {},
  ): Promise<Provider> {
    const descriptorBytes = options.descriptorBytes ?? TRUSTED_DESCRIPTOR_BYTES;
    const bindingBytes = options.bindingBytes ?? TRUSTED_BINDING_BYTES;
    // This consumer's OWN independent replay, before any Wasm allocation at
    // all -- a consumer that only trusted the loaded module's own answer
    // would defeat the point of an independently verified descriptor.
    verifyDescriptorAndBinding(descriptorBytes, bindingBytes);

    let instance: WebAssembly.Instance;
    if (moduleOrBytes instanceof WebAssembly.Module) {
      // A caller-supplied, already-compiled `Module` carries no recoverable
      // byte representation through the platform `WebAssembly` API, so
      // this path cannot verify a provider-artifact digest -- a real,
      // stated platform limitation, not a shortcut. A caller who needs the
      // digest check must supply `BufferSource` bytes instead.
      instance = await WebAssembly.instantiate(moduleOrBytes, {});
    } else {
      const bytes = toBytes(moduleOrBytes);
      await verifyModuleArtifactDigest(bytes);
      const result = await WebAssembly.instantiate(bytes, {});
      instance = result.instance;
    }

    const memoryExport = instance.exports["memory"];
    if (!(memoryExport instanceof WebAssembly.Memory)) {
      throw new SemapraxPublicGenericException({
        kind: "provider-mismatch",
        reason:
          'the module does not export a real WebAssembly.Memory named "memory"',
      });
    }
    const endpointExport = instance.exports[TRUSTED_ENDPOINT_EXPORT_NAME];
    if (typeof endpointExport !== "function") {
      throw new SemapraxPublicGenericException({
        kind: "provider-mismatch",
        reason: "the module does not export the trusted endpoint function",
      });
    }
    return new Provider(memoryExport, endpointExport as EndpointFn);
  }

  #requireLive(): void {
    if (this.#state === "closed") {
      throw carrierRejected("called after close");
    }
  }

  #checkInjected(ordinal: FailureOrdinal): void {
    if (this.#injected === ordinal) {
      this.#injected = null;
      throw new SemapraxPublicGenericException({
        kind: "execution-failed",
        status: ordinal,
      });
    }
  }

  /** Stage one owned input: allocate a bounded span, copy the exact carrier
   * bytes into it, and register an input-root handle. Never holds a view
   * across the allocation itself (a fresh view is taken only after `alloc`
   * returns). Private: the public production surface is `transform` alone
   * ("If the public API exposes only transform(input), keep handle
   * wrappers private" -- issue #157's own requirement); `Provider.diagnostics`
   * below exposes this same real method to `test/round-trip.mjs` for
   * hostile-state exercises. */
  #prepareInput(input: Input): OpaqueHandle {
    this.#requireLive();
    const carrier = encodeInput(input);
    this.#checkInjected(FAILURE_ORDINALS.AFTER_INPUT_VALIDATED);

    const callId = this.#nextGeneration;
    this.#nextGeneration += 1;
    const offset = this.#allocator.alloc(carrier.length);
    try {
      this.#checkInjected(FAILURE_ORDINALS.AFTER_INPUT_ALLOCATED);
      this.#allocator.view().set(carrier, offset);
      this.#checkInjected(FAILURE_ORDINALS.AFTER_INPUT_WRITTEN);
    } catch (error) {
      this.#allocator.dealloc(offset, carrier.length);
      throw error;
    }
    this.#registry.insert(0, callId, {
      role: "input-root",
      offset,
      length: carrier.length,
    });
    this.#calls.set(callId, { stage: "pending-value" });
    return OpaqueHandle.mint(0, callId, this.#tag);
  }

  /** Commit input transfer, call the real endpoint export once per leaf
   * in place over real linear memory, physically release the consumed
   * input (always -- before any result is ever published), commit a fresh
   * result span, and return its handle. Private; see `#prepareInput`. */
  #call(handle: OpaqueHandle): OpaqueHandle {
    this.#requireLive();
    if (!handle.belongsTo(this.#tag)) {
      throw carrierRejected("handle does not belong to this provider");
    }
    const callId = handle.generation();
    const entry = this.#registry.remove(handle.id(), callId, "input-root");
    const state = this.#calls.get(callId);
    if (state === undefined || state.stage !== "pending-value") {
      throw carrierRejected("handle names a call that is not pending a value");
    }

    let inputReleased = false;
    try {
      const carrierView = this.#allocator
        .view()
        .slice(entry.offset, entry.offset + entry.length);
      const spans = locateLeaves(carrierView, FIELD_COUNT);
      for (const span of spans) {
        // Real Wasm execution: the export mutates real linear memory in
        // place at an absolute offset this host computed and bounds-checked
        // itself (`locateLeaves` already validated every span against the
        // decoded carrier length).
        this.#endpoint(entry.offset + span.offset, span.length);
      }
      this.#checkInjected(FAILURE_ORDINALS.AFTER_ENDPOINT_CALLED);

      const reversedLeaves = spans.map((span) => {
        const absolute = entry.offset + span.offset;
        // A fresh copy, not a live view: this array survives the
        // deallocation (and zeroing) immediately below.
        return this.#allocator.view().slice(absolute, absolute + span.length);
      });

      // Non-result obligation: release the consumed input before the
      // result is ever published, success or failure -- restates
      // `WasmProvider::call`'s own release ordering (see
      // `wasm/provider.rs`'s module documentation) without sharing any code
      // with it.
      this.#allocator.dealloc(entry.offset, entry.length);
      inputReleased = true;
      this.#checkInjected(FAILURE_ORDINALS.AFTER_INPUT_RELEASED);

      const resultCarrier = encodeLeaves(reversedLeaves);
      const resultOffset = this.#allocator.alloc(resultCarrier.length);
      try {
        this.#checkInjected(FAILURE_ORDINALS.AFTER_RESULT_ALLOCATED);
        this.#allocator.view().set(resultCarrier, resultOffset);
        this.#checkInjected(FAILURE_ORDINALS.AFTER_RESULT_WRITTEN);
      } catch (error) {
        this.#allocator.dealloc(resultOffset, resultCarrier.length);
        throw error;
      }
      this.#registry.insert(RESULT_ID_OFFSET, callId, {
        role: "result-root",
        offset: resultOffset,
        length: resultCarrier.length,
      });
      state.stage = "pending-result";
      return OpaqueHandle.mint(RESULT_ID_OFFSET, callId, this.#tag);
    } catch (error) {
      if (!inputReleased) {
        // The registry entry was already removed above (before any of this
        // could fail); only the physical allocation might still be live.
        try {
          this.#allocator.dealloc(entry.offset, entry.length);
        } catch {
          // A cleanup failure during unwind is secondary and must not hide
          // the primary error already being thrown.
        }
      }
      this.#calls.delete(callId);
      throw error;
    }
  }

  /** Copy the committed result out of real Wasm memory into a fresh
   * JS-owned `Uint8Array`, and independently decode it. Never exposes a
   * live memory view: `.slice()` always copies. Private; see
   * `#prepareInput`. */
  #exportResult(handle: OpaqueHandle): Output {
    this.#requireLive();
    if (!handle.belongsTo(this.#tag)) {
      throw carrierRejected("handle does not belong to this provider");
    }
    const entry = this.#registry.get(
      handle.id(),
      handle.generation(),
      "result-root",
    );
    const exported = this.#allocator
      .view()
      .slice(entry.offset, entry.offset + entry.length);
    const output = decodeOutput(exported);
    this.#checkInjected(FAILURE_ORDINALS.AFTER_RESULT_COPIED_OUT);
    return output;
  }

  /** Release a fully exported (or not-yet-exported) result handle.
   * Private; see `#prepareInput`. */
  #releaseResult(handle: OpaqueHandle): void {
    if (!handle.belongsTo(this.#tag)) {
      throw carrierRejected("handle does not belong to this provider");
    }
    const callId = handle.generation();
    const entry = this.#registry.remove(handle.id(), callId, "result-root");
    this.#allocator.dealloc(entry.offset, entry.length);
    this.#calls.delete(callId);
  }

  /** Release a value handle before it is ever passed to `#call` (an
   * abandoned call). A handle already consumed by `#call`, or already
   * released, is simply not live and fails closed. Private; see
   * `#prepareInput`. */
  #releaseInput(handle: OpaqueHandle): void {
    if (!handle.belongsTo(this.#tag)) {
      throw carrierRejected("handle does not belong to this provider");
    }
    const callId = handle.generation();
    const entry = this.#registry.remove(handle.id(), callId, "input-root");
    this.#allocator.dealloc(entry.offset, entry.length);
    this.#calls.delete(callId);
  }

  /** The full round trip: encode, stage, call, export, release -- always,
   * success or failure. This is the only entry point the generated
   * package's own `index.ts` re-exports. */
  transform(input: Input): Output {
    const inputHandle = this.#prepareInput(input);
    let resultHandle: OpaqueHandle | null = null;
    try {
      resultHandle = this.#call(inputHandle);
      const output = this.#exportResult(resultHandle);
      this.#releaseResult(resultHandle);
      resultHandle = null;
      return output;
    } finally {
      if (resultHandle !== null) {
        try {
          this.#releaseResult(resultHandle);
        } catch {
          // Secondary cleanup failure during unwind; never hides the
          // primary error already propagating.
        }
      }
    }
  }

  /** Refuses to close with any live handle, matching
   * `WasmProvider::close`. */
  close(): void {
    if (this.#state === "closed") {
      return;
    }
    if (this.#registry.size() !== 0 || this.#calls.size !== 0) {
      throw new SemapraxPublicGenericException({
        kind: "release-failed",
        status: -1,
      });
    }
    this.#state = "closed";
  }

  /** Test-only settlement-proof surface. Never part of any production or
   * publication claim -- see this file's own module banner. Exists solely
   * so `test/round-trip.mjs` can prove zero live allocations/handles after
   * every terminal case, and can exercise hostile handle states through
   * this same real implementation rather than a second stand-in. */
  static readonly diagnostics = {
    liveAllocations(provider: Provider): number {
      return provider.#allocator.liveAllocations();
    },
    liveHandles(provider: Provider): number {
      return provider.#registry.size();
    },
    injectFailure(provider: Provider, ordinal: FailureOrdinal): void {
      provider.#injected = ordinal;
    },
    clearFailureInjection(provider: Provider): void {
      provider.#injected = null;
    },
    foreignHandle(id: number, generation: number): OpaqueHandle {
      // Minted with a tag no real `Provider` ever holds -- `belongsTo`
      // always fails for it, proving a handle from a different provider
      // (or a hostile mint attempt) is rejected rather than silently
      // accepted.
      return OpaqueHandle.mint(id, generation, {});
    },
    // The same private, real methods `transform` composes, exposed only so
    // `test/round-trip.mjs` can exercise hostile intermediate states
    // (stale/foreign/wrong-role/double-released handles) without a second,
    // parallel implementation.
    prepareInput(provider: Provider, input: Input): OpaqueHandle {
      return provider.#prepareInput(input);
    },
    call(provider: Provider, handle: OpaqueHandle): OpaqueHandle {
      return provider.#call(handle);
    },
    exportResult(provider: Provider, handle: OpaqueHandle): Output {
      return provider.#exportResult(handle);
    },
    releaseResult(provider: Provider, handle: OpaqueHandle): void {
      provider.#releaseResult(handle);
    },
    releaseInput(provider: Provider, handle: OpaqueHandle): void {
      provider.#releaseInput(handle);
    },
  };
}

function toBytes(source: BufferSource): Uint8Array {
  if (source instanceof Uint8Array) {
    return source;
  }
  if (source instanceof ArrayBuffer) {
    return new Uint8Array(source);
  }
  // Every other `BufferSource` is a typed array or `DataView` over some
  // `ArrayBufferLike`; copy its exact viewed span.
  return new Uint8Array(source.buffer, source.byteOffset, source.byteLength);
}
